# proxy-usage-analysis: consume actor/source/reason attribution from proxy restart logs

## Goal

Teach the proxy-usage-analysis tooling to consume the attribution markers added
by **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** (actor/source/reason on mode-switch and `--restart`
log lines) so restart attribution appears in the generated reports and the
mode-timeline classification stops being heuristic.

## Context

**LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** adds structured attribution to the proxy logs
(`source=scheduler|worker|api|manual`, `actor`, `reason`, requested `mode`) at
`set_mode()` time and to `start-proxy.sh --restart` startup output. Its AC3
proves attribution with a reproducible grep only; the reporting/parsing stack
(`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`, `bucketing.py`,
`reporting.py`) and `scripts/analyze_mode_flips.py` still classify restart
causes heuristically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `log_parser.py` parses the new attribution markers into structured fields
      on the restart/mode-switch events (absent markers degrade gracefully to
      the current behaviour).
- [ ] `bucketing.py` / `reporting.py` surface the attribution (source + actor +
      reason) in the mode-timeline / restart report sections.
- [ ] `scripts/analyze_mode_flips.py` uses `source` to classify flips instead of
      heuristics where the marker is present.
- [ ] Unit tests cover parsing of the new markers (present + absent) and the
      report output.
- [ ] A report generated from logs containing the new markers shows zero
      "unknown/ unattributable" restarts that carry a marker.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Depends on **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** landing first (markers must exist).
- Backward compatible: must still parse historical logs without the markers.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH** — Log the requesting actor and reason for every proxy
  mode-switch / `--restart` so restarts are always attributable
  (`discovered-from`).
- **LP-0MT1EE315007AKXG** — proxy-usage-analysis: recognise manual mode switches
  in the mode timeline.
data.title: proxy-usage-analysis: consume actor/source/reason attribution from proxy restart logs

## Problem statement

The refactor skill filed an `E741` ("ambiguous variable name: `l`") finding at
line 4756 of `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
and injected a `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker. Investigation shows the
finding is a **false positive**: no committed revision of the file has ever
contained an `l` identifier, and `ruff check` on the current file passes.

## Users

- **Maintainers of the proxy-usage-analysis skill** — need a worklog that does
  not carry phantom technical debt.
- **The refactor skill / future lint sweeps** — need accurate detection; stale
  markers suppress future findings for the same smell type in this file.

User stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the worklog to reflect real defects so triage time is
  not spent re-verifying already-clean code.
- As an agent running `/skill:refactor`, I want a stale `REFACTOR` marker to be
  removed once its smell no longer exists, so the marker does not mask new
  findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ruff check --select E741 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` reports no findings.
- [ ] An AST scan (or equivalent) confirms no `Name`/`arg` identifier equal to `l` (or the other E741 names `O`/`I`) exists in the file.
- [ ] The work item's disposition is recorded in a comment: either **closed as resolved-in-parent** (smell fixed before parent commit `c0f3625f`, no code change) or the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block is removed from the file.
- [ ] Testing/validation criterion: the verification commands above are documented in the work item so a reviewer can reproduce the conclusion.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The finding references a **deleted worktree path**
  (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4-surface-attribution-in-reporting-py/`);
  the authoritative file is the main checkout copy.
- `AGENTS.md` repository boundaries: `.pi/` must not be edited unless
  explicitly instructed — removing the marker requires explicit authorisation.
- The repo already carries other stale `REFACTOR` markers (e.g.
  `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` in the same file, `LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA`,
  `LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G`); a one-off removal would be inconsistent without the
  systemic fix.

## Existing state

- Current HEAD file: 5,023 lines; line 4756 is the docstring
  `"""LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4 — attribution surfaces in the report."""` — a docstring,
  not a variable.
- Every committed revision (40 commits touching the file) checked: zero
  standalone `l` identifiers. `git log -S "for l in"` returns nothing.
- `ruff check` on the file: **All checks passed!**
- AST scan for `Name`/`arg` in `{l, O, I}`: **NONE**.
- The parent item `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` ("Surface attribution in reporting.py")
  is `completed`/`done`; its commit `c0f3625f` is the one that both injected the
  marker and (evidently) landed the fixed file — so the smell was resolved in
  the same session, before commit.

## Desired change

Minimal: record the false-positive/resolved-in-parent disposition and close the
item. Optional (requires explicit authorisation under the `.pi/` boundary
rule): delete the six-line `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block so the
`formatting` smell type is no longer suppressed for this file.

Systemic follow-up (out of scope, filed as `discovered-from`): the refactor
skill should remove a `REFACTOR` marker when its work item is closed — it
currently only injects (`comment_injection.py` has no removal path), so stale
markers accumulate repo-wide.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — lines 1–6 hold the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block (optional removal).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixtures used by the file; no change expected.
- `.ruff.toml` — confirms `E` (incl. `E741`) is selected and not ignored; no change expected.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` — Surface attribution in reporting.py (parent session that injected the marker; completed).
- `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` — Refactor: unused variable `schedule`, same file/marker mechanism (completed; marker still present).
- `LP-0MU1I7T37001CV4O` — ruff I001 candidate false positive at another file (closed as duplicate of an already-fixed parent finding; disposition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the `l` variable existed only in the pre-commit worktree state
  and was fixed before `c0f3625f`; the worktree is deleted, so this cannot be
  re-verified directly. Evidence: the marker was committed by the same commit
  that landed the corrected file.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "also clean up every stale REFACTOR marker" — record
  as a linked work item, not as scope here.
- **Risk:** removing the marker alone does not fix the systemic leak; without
  the systemic item, stale markers will keep accumulating.
- **Risk:** misclassifying a real finding as false positive. Mitigated by the
  reproducible AST + ruff checks in the ACs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is this E741 finding real, or a false positive?" — Answer (Map, evidence-based): **False positive.** No committed revision contains an `l` identifier; `ruff check` passes; AST scan finds no `l`/`O`/`I` names. Source: `git log --all -S "for l in"` (empty), `ruff check` on the file, AST walk of current HEAD, inspection of commit `c0f3625f`. Evidence path: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:4756`.
- Q: "Should the stale `REFACTOR` marker be removed as part of this item?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION for the producer.** Recommended: close as resolved-in-parent without touching `.pi/` (respects the repository-boundaries rule); file a separate `discovered-from` item for the systemic marker-removal gap. Source: agent recommendation, pending operator confirmation.

# Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator, I want a mechanism to restrict which clients may claim high (or any non-default) request priority, so the priority-routing feature cannot be defeated by every client marking every request `X-Priority: high`.

## Background

The priority-routing epic (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA) ships v1 with **no trust gate** (decision d from intake): the header is honoured from any reachable client. This item tracks the hardening follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft)

- A configurable gate restricts who may request priority above `medium` (e.g. trusted-source allowlist of localhost/subnets, shared-secret header, or per-client capability map).
- Unauthorised high-priority claims are silently downgraded to `medium` (no error, no DoS by 4xx) and logged.
- Choice of gate mechanism documented in the epic's appendix; gate is off by default until operator opts in.
- All related documentation updated and full project test suite passes.
data.title: Priority header trust gate: authenticate/authorize X-Priority before trusting it (spoofing risk)

# Limiter skip log prints an impossible ratio when the reserve is in use

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Problem

`SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` logs the rejection ratio as
`len(window)/max_rpm`, but with the free-tier reserve
(`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) the per-caller cap can be lower than the number of
entries already in the window, producing log lines that look like a bug:

```
WARNING - Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 10/7 requests in 60s window
WARNING - Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=7 reserve=3 ...
```

The `10` is the count in the window (including slots taken by in-progress
sessions), the `7` is the cap applied to this new-session request. Operators and
log analyses read `10/7` as an arithmetic error.

## Desired change

Make the message self-describing, e.g.:

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: window=10 cap=7 (reserve in use) requests in 60s window
```

Keep the emitted fields parseable (stable `key=value` tokens) so the
proxy-usage / budget-effectiveness analyses can extract `window=` and `cap=`
instead of inferring them from provider config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rejection log line names both the in-window count and the cap applied to
  the rejected request, with no value that can read as `count/cap` confusion.
- A unit test asserts the emitted message contains `window=`, `cap=` and the
  correct numbers for (a) a plain over-limit rejection and (b) a
  reserve-limited rejection (cap < window count).
- No behaviour change: only the message text (and any consumed parse) changes;
  full project test suite passes.
data.title: Limiter skip log prints 10/7 when the reserve is in use

# Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want **one** authoritative description of the provider
fallback model — every knob that shapes a chain, the layer it applies at
(provider entry / model / server), and the order those layers win in — so I can
answer "how do I control X for model Y?" without reading `provider.py`, and so
new controls (e.g. per-model budget knobs, `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) slot into a
documented contract instead of inventing a new shape.

Low priority: documentation/consolidation only, no behaviour change.

## Current state (fragmented)

Fallback behaviour is described in five places that have drifted apart:
`proxy/config.yaml` header comments, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`,
`proxy/docs/routing.md` and inline code comments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` /
`provider_budget.py`. The knobs themselves are spread across three layers with
no single statement of precedence:

| Layer | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Provider entry | `rate_limit_rpm`, `available_times`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `forward_session_headers`, `api`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | per-entry, order defines chain position |
| Model (`models.<name>`) | `providers` list order, `aliases`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | one model key → one chain, shared by all aliases |
| Server (`server.*`) | `provider_cooldown_seconds`, `sibling_fallback_*`, `chain_hold_*`, `upstream_*`, `provider_rate_limit_*`, `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, `max_retry_after_seconds` | global; some are inherited-only across mode overlays |
| Mode overlay | `config-fast.yaml`, `config-cheap.yaml` | lists replace wholesale; other values replace; only diffs declared |
| Runtime | cooldowns, usage-limit quarantine, stall circuit breaker, affinity records, budget windows | in-memory + `proxy/provider-state.json` |

Cross-cutting semantics that are easy to get wrong and belong in one place:
failure-domain grouping (shared endpoint+model), per-account vs per-endpoint
exclusion, time windows (`available_times`), the free-tier budget gate
(`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) including the reserve and
affinity, chain-hold retry cycles, sibling-fallback circuit breaker,
mode grandfathering, and which of these reset on proxy restart (in-memory vs
persisted).

## Desired change

1. A single reference document (e.g. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`)
   covering: chain resolution order, every knob with its layer + default +
   precedence, the failure/cooldown/quarantine taxonomies, quota/budget gating,
   mode overlays and grandfathering, and what is persisted vs in-memory.
2. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to it instead of duplicating
   the detail (keep short, task-focused sections there).
3. A short "inconsistencies / gaps" section recording anything found while
   writing it (knobs only available globally, provider lists duplicated in the
   fast overlay, budget gating only on one entry, etc.) — recorded as
   `discovered-from` work items rather than fixed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` exists and states, for every
   fallback-related knob: name, layer, default, precedence, and the behaviour it
   controls — verified against the code paths that read it (no invented values).
2. A precedence table covers entry > model (where applicable) > server >
   built-in default, including the mode-overlay merge rule (lists replace,
   scalars replace, dicts merge) and the `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` inheritance
   contract.
3. The persistence section distinguishes state that survives a restart
   (`provider-state.json`, grandfathered bindings) from in-memory state
   (cooldowns, stall breaker, affinity, budget windows).
4. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to the new document and no
   longer contradict it.
5. Every inconsistency found is either fixed by a linked `discovered-from` item
   or explicitly recorded as accepted.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments where a pointer to the new document replaces duplicated prose.
7. Full project test suite passes (documentation-only change must not perturb
   behaviour).

## Constraints

- Documentation/analysis only: no behaviour, config-value or code-path changes in
  this item.
- Do not duplicate the new budget-gate material — reference
  `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` / `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` and the per-model controls item
  (`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) rather than restating their designs.
- UK English, Markdown, no secrets (reference API keys by env-var name only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` — new reference document.
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — link + trim
  duplicated material.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — header comments point at the document.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — verify claims;
  replace duplicated comments with pointers only where clearly redundant.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` — per-model budget knobs (the contract this document
  should describe once it lands).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — the free-tier budget gate,
  reserve and wait cap.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — whether `rate_limit_rpm` should be raised.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived budgeting.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — free tier restricted to cheap mode.
data.title: Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

# Per-model token summary section in /logs summary header

## Summary

Extend the `/logs` page summary header (`renderSummary()` in `view_logs.html`) with a per-model token section aggregating token-count keys by model name. Each row shows a model's total sent/recv tokens and the per-category breakdown (User, Assistant, Tool, System sent; Response recv). Keys without a model suffix group under "unknown". Pure client-side change — no server, schema, or persistence changes.

## Problem Statement

Operators cannot see per-model aggregate token usage (a key cost/capacity signal); the `/logs` header currently breaks tokens down per endpoint only. Model names are recoverable from existing token-count key suffixes (`-> model:<name>` and bare `model:<name>`), so grouping is a client-side aggregation over the existing SSE snapshot with no new counting logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `/logs` page summary header displays a per-model token section (in addition to the existing per-endpoint section), rendered by `renderSummary()` in `view_logs.html`, with one row per distinct model showing total sent (input) and total recv (output) tokens.
- Model names are extracted from existing token-count keys via the `-> model:<name>` suffix (and bare `model:<name>` keys) already present in token-count keys such as `sent:user:POST /v1/chat/completions -> model:qwen3.6`; multiple endpoint paths sharing a model aggregate into one row.
- Running totals accumulate across requests and persist across proxy restarts via the existing `token_counts` JSON file (`proxy/logs/token_counts.json`); no schema, persistence-path, or load/save change.
- The per-model summary renders within the existing `renderSummary()` JavaScript function in `view_logs.html`, using the same SSE snapshot format (`{"tokens": {...}}`).
- Each model row shows the per-category breakdown consistent with existing category keys: User, Assistant, Tool Calls, System Prompt (sent) and Response (recv).
- Keys without a model suffix are grouped under an "unknown" row (with a console-level debug note) rather than dropped or misattributed.
- The existing per-endpoint token section remains unchanged; no double-counting between the per-endpoint and per-model views.
- No server-side changes: same SSE snapshot format is consumed; `token_counts.json` schema, persistence path, and load/save behaviour are unchanged.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new server-side token-counting logic; grouping is purely client-side.
- Backward compatible with existing and legacy keys (both suffixed and unsuffixed).
- UI stays usable with many models (scrollable container acceptable; no charts/export in scope).

## Key Files

- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — `renderSummary()` gains the per-model aggregation block

## Assumptions

- The model name in the key suffix is stable and sufficient for grouping (no model registry lookup).
- `/logs` page is the sole UI target.
- Legacy keys (`-> local` / `-> remote` / unsuffixed) are tolerated and grouped under "unknown".
data.title: Per-model token summary section in /logs summary header

## Goal

Prove on real traffic that the all-opencode off-peak low chain absorbs local-slot overflow, and that it neither widens paid spend outside the windows nor regresses the free tier.

## Work

1. **Baseline** (pre-change window) via the proxy-usage-analysis skill CLI:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`
   Record: `rate_limited`, `fallback_after_queue`, `empty_response`, HTTP 429/503 counts, per-model token share, `munitoai-free` share.
2. After one full 24 h window post-change, re-run the same CLI and diff the same metrics.
3. In `proxy.log`, confirm `Fallback triggered ... to=opencode-go*` events for low-priority traffic occur **only** inside the `available_times` windows, and **zero** inside the UTC 01:00–04:00 / 06:00–10:00 gaps.
4. Confirm the three opencode keys each received traffic (i.e. per-key failover actually engages), by counting dispatches per `api_key_env`.
5. Comment the parent item (LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX) with the before/after table and verdict.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Before/after metrics table recorded on the parent work item.
2. Log evidence of at least one low-priority fallback to an opencode entry inside an off-peak window — or a documented reason none occurred (e.g. local never overflowed in that window).
3. **Zero** low-priority opencode fallbacks inside the UTC gap windows (01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00) — proving no paid spend leaked outside permissible times.
4. Per-key dispatch counts show whether more than one opencode key was used; if only one was used, say whether that reflects no 429s or an unexpected exclusion bug.
5. Explicit cost statement: did paid-tier token share rise outside the overlap hours? Yes = regression, record it.
6. Honest sample-size caveat when the window is too small to move aggregate numbers.
data.title: Verify off-peak low-priority fallback in a live window

# Configuration keys and quota-surge design doc

## Goal

Make the feature self-documenting: every new `server.*` key carries its
default and rationale in `config.yaml`, and `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` explains
the pacing model, the peak/off-peak trade-off and the per-account
(non-calendar) reset caveat.

## Scope

- `proxy/config.yaml`: document every new key added by the implementation
  features, each with its default and a short rationale comment:
  - `quota_surge_enabled` [true]
  - `quota_surge_dry_run` [false]
  - `quota_poll_interval_seconds` [900]
  - `quota_surge_days` [7]
  - `quota_exhaustion_percent` [99.5]
  - `quota_state_max_age_seconds` [3600]
  - `quota_pacing_target` [0.95]
  - `quota_surge_accounts` (optional filter; default all `opencode-*`)
- `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` covering:
  - The problem (use-it-or-lose-it allowances; per-account, non-calendar
    `resetsAt`; observed 88% / 95% / 5% spread).
  - The `/v1/usage` contract discovered live (shape, `no-store`, no headers,
    no model selector, no credits endpoint) and its graceful-degradation
    requirements.
  - The derivation model (headroom = 100 − percent; effective headroom = min of
    rolling/weekly/monthly) and why the minimum, not the monthly figure,
    governs eligibility.
  - The pacing/scoring model: `score = effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`,
    the achievability argument against the rolling (20%) and weekly (50%) caps,
    and why the ramp may start before the final week.
  - The peak/off-peak trade-off: peak DeepSeek windows (`01:00-04:00`,
    `06:00-10:00` UTC Mon–Fri) burn the dollar allowance at 2x, so surge only
    escalates to peak when the residual is otherwise unspendable.
  - Safety: hard stop at `quota_exhaustion_percent`, kill switch, dry-run,
    stale-state fail-safe, and the explicit statement that surge bypasses
    `available_times` only.
  - Operational runbook: how to disable quickly, how to read the new metrics,
    and how to confirm surge is working after deploy.
- Keep `proxy/config_test.yaml` valid; add a test asserting the documented
  defaults parse and that every new key is read with the documented default
  when absent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC12 — Documentation: `proxy/config.yaml` comments for every new key (with
  documented defaults) and `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` describing the model, the
  peak-pricing caveat and the per-account (non-calendar) reset dates.
- AC12b — `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` documents the pacing/scoring model
  (`effective_headroom / seconds_to_reset`), the rolling/weekly achievability
  argument, the kill switch/dry-run/stale-state guards, and the operational
  runbook for disabling the feature.
- AC12c — A test asserts every documented key parses from `proxy/config.yaml`
  and that the code falls back to the documented default when a key is absent,
  so documentation cannot drift from behaviour.
- AC12d — No documented behaviour claims a guarantee the tests do not cover
  (the cross-check between the doc's claims and the test suite is recorded as
  a review note on this item).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the key comments in `proxy/config.yaml` next to the existing
   provider-budget/chain-hold documentation.
2. Write `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` following the structure above.
3. Add `proxy/tests/test_quota_config_docs.py` reading `proxy/config.yaml`
   with `yaml.safe_load` and asserting defaults/parseability.
4. Cross-check each documented claim against an existing test name and note
   gaps as follow-ups rather than silent omissions.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/config_test.yaml`
- `docs/dev/quota-surge.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_config_docs.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Pacing model: urgency score and cap achievability`.
- Depends on `Headroom-aware opencode chain ordering`.
- Depends on `Final-week available_times surge bypass`.

# End-to-end integration test and regression gate

## Goal

Prove the whole feature works as one flow — poll, derive, order, surge, hard
stop, stale revert — against a fake upstream, and prove the existing suite is
unaffected before the epic goes to review.

## Scope

- One integration test that stands up a fake upstream HTTP server serving both
  `GET /v1/usage` and `POST /v1/chat/completions`, wires the proxy's provider
  resolution to it, and drives a representative request sequence:
  1. Three `opencode-*` accounts with the observed live percentages
     (88% / 95% / 5%) → dispatch goes to the 5% account.
  2. Advance the clock into an account's final week → the bypass becomes
     active and the dispatch is allowed outside its `available_times` window,
     with `reason=quota_surge` logged once.
  3. Cross the hard stop (99.6%) mid-surge → the account is skipped on the
     very next dispatch with zero further upstream calls.
  4. Age the snapshot past `quota_state_max_age_seconds` → surge suspended,
     routing reverts to configured `available_times`.
- A regression assertion that the pre-existing suites covering
  `available_times`, chain fallback, usage-limit quarantine and provider
  budget still pass unchanged.
- Add a short "Test map" section to the parent work item linking each parent
  AC to the test that proves it (used by the audit/coverage review).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC11 — Tests cover the poller, derivation, ordering, bypass, pacing, guards
  and kill switch (unit + at least one integration test against a fake
  upstream), all green, and the existing suite is unaffected.
- AC11b — The integration test drives a full dispatch through a fake `/v1/usage`
  and fake `chat/completions` upstream, exercising surge, ordering, hard stop
  and stale-state in a single flow with no live network access.
- AC11c — The full suite is green through the test skill
  (`run_tests.py`) at the feature-branch head, with the changed-scope gate
  passing before the commit.
- AC11d — A test-to-AC map (in the parent work item) shows at least one
  passing test for every parent acceptance criterion AC1–AC13b.

## Minimal implementation

1. Reuse the poller test harness from the tracer bullet; add the fake
   chat-completions upstream in `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_integration.py`.
2. Drive dispatch through the real resolution functions with a stubbed
   transport/proxy layer (no live sockets to opencode.ai).
3. Run the changed-scope gate before committing, then the full suite for the
   push gate.
4. Record the test-to-AC map in the parent item.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_integration.py`
- `proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/quota_state.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Headroom-aware opencode chain ordering`.
- Depends on `Final-week available_times surge bypass`.
- Depends on `Quota hard stop and cost guard`.
- Depends on `Stale-state fail-safe, kill switch and dry-run`.
- Depends on `Quota observability surface`.
- Sequencing note: final verification slice; must not start until the
  behaviour features are merged into the branch.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_integration.py` (end-to-end flow)
- Regression evidence for the existing suites
- Test-to-AC map recorded on the parent item

## Test plan

- The four-step flow above, each step asserted independently so a failure
  names the phase.
- Assert zero upstream calls after the hard stop.
- Assert WARN/INFO log records for surge transitions and stale suspension
  (using `caplog`).
- Full suite green; no skipped tests added by this epic without a recorded
  reason.

# Post-deploy allowance-utilisation measurement

## Goal

Close the loop on the epic's actual outcome: measure, per account, how much of
the monthly allowance was spent at the moment of reset for the first full
period after deployment, and tune the defaults if the target is missed.

## Scope

- Build a log-derived report reusing the existing
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis` CLI (deterministic, no ad-hoc parsing):
  - For each `opencode-*` account, the monthly percentage reading closest to
    (and immediately before) its `resetsAt` for the first full period after
    deployment.
  - The residual at reset (100 − percent), and whether surge was active in the
    final days of the period.
  - Time spent at the hard stop, and any quota-driven skips.
- Target: ≥ 90% monthly consumption at reset per account (the ≤ 10% residual is
  the safety margin needed for the rolling 20% / weekly 50% caps).
- Output: `docs/dev/quota-surge-post-deploy-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` plus a machine-
  readable JSON alongside it, referenced from this item.
- If any account finishes below 90%, record a follow-up work item proposing a
  concrete tuning change (e.g. `quota_pacing_target`, `quota_surge_days`,
  ramp start) with the observed data attached.
- If an account hits 100% (or the hard stop is crossed upward) record a
  critical follow-up immediately — that is the overspend path the guard exists
  to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC13 — Post-deploy measurement: a log-derived report (reusing
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`) shows, per account, the monthly percentage
  at the moment of reset for the first full period after deployment, with a
  target of ≥ 90%.
- AC13b — The report is committed as `docs/dev/quota-surge-post-deploy-<date>.md`
  plus a JSON data file, and linked from this work item with the per-account
  outcome and any tuning recommendation.
- AC13c — Below-target accounts produce a follow-up work item with the tuning
  proposal and the observed data attached; any account at or above the hard
  stop produces a critical `test-failure`/overspend follow-up instead of a
  silent note.
- AC13d — The measurement is reproducible: the exact CLI invocation (arguments,
  log window, filters) is recorded in the report so the operator can re-run it
  for the next period.

## Minimal implementation

1. Wait for one full billing period after deployment (per-account reset dates
   are not calendar-aligned — schedule per account).
2. Run the `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis` CLI over the period's logs with a
   recorded invocation.
3. Extract per-account percent at reset and surge activity; write the Markdown
   + JSON report under `docs/dev/`.
4. Record the outcome on this item and open follow-ups per the rules above.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/quota-surge-post-deploy-2026-11-23.md`
- `docs/dev/quota-surge-post-deploy-2026-11-23.json`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on `End-to-end integration test and regression gate`.
- Note: deliberately time-gated — it cannot complete until a full reset period
  has elapsed after the epic ships.

## Deliverables

- Per-account allowance-utilisation report for the first full period
- JSON data file with the raw measurements
- Follow-up work items where the target is missed or the hard stop is crossed

## Test plan

- Verify the report's numbers against a manual spot-check for one account
  (percent at a known timestamp) so the derived figure is trustworthy.
- Confirm the recorded CLI invocation re-runs cleanly and reproduces the same
  figures from the same logs.
data.title: Post-deploy allowance-utilisation measurement
